implemented_capabilities: app/action_contracts.py + contracts/action-request.schema.json: ActiveWindowContext extended (additive, backward-compatible) with window_state (normal/minimized/maximized/unknown), monitor (geometry + is_primary, no pixel data), focused_control (control-type/name/automation-id/class-name metadata only, name redacted for IsPassword controls), and source (win32/ui_automation). actions/requests.py's ActionRequestFactory field allowlists (_ALLOWED_CONTEXT_FIELDS, plus new _ALLOWED_MONITOR_FIELDS/_ALLOWED_FOCUSED_CONTROL_FIELDS) extended in lockstep so the defense-in-depth allowlist can't silently drift from the schema/model. selected_text and clipboard content are deliberately NOT fields on this struct -- they are returned only by explicit, individually-audited read actions (read_selected_text/read_clipboard), never attached silently to unrelated ActionRequests.

skills/_desktop_automation.py: real Windows UI Automation + win32 helpers (uiautomation/comtypes, not pywinauto). resolve_window() (foreground window, or executable/title match reusing windows_app._find_window), capture_window_state/capture_monitor/capture_window_bounds/capture_focused_control_info (all metadata-only), build_active_window_context() (the full rich-context builder), serialize_control()/walk_actionable_controls() (bounded BFS: depth-capped, count-capped [default 100, hard max 300], and separately visit-capped against pathological trees), ControlHandleCache (TTL 180s / max 400 entries, oldest-evicted -- bounded, not indefinite raw-UI-tree retention), read_selected_text() (TextPattern.GetSelection, refuses IsPassword controls), read_clipboard_text() (win32clipboard CF_UNICODETEXT, returns None -- not an error -- when no text format is present), and do_focus/do_invoke/do_type/do_select/do_scroll (each driving a real UIA pattern: Invoke/Toggle/LegacyIAccessiblePattern for invoke; ValuePattern/LegacyIAccessiblePattern for type; SelectionItemPattern/LegacyIAccessiblePattern for select; ScrollPattern for scroll -- no blind-coordinate clicking, no keystroke simulation, per the spec).

skills/desktop_control.py (DesktopControlSkill, capabilities: inspect_current_window, list_controls, focus_control, invoke_control, type_into_control, select_control, scroll_control, read_selected_text, read_clipboard): inspect_current_window is the bounded context-snapshot primitive (active window incl. new metadata fields, up to max_controls visible actionable controls [default 20, hard-capped 50], best-effort selected text, clipboard text only when include_clipboard=true is explicitly passed -- ephemeral, returned in ActionResult.data, not cached server-side). list_controls enumerates a target window's actionable controls with a stable-enough opaque control_id per element. focus_control/invoke_control/type_into_control/select_control/scroll_control act on a previously-listed control_id, each returning a real, honest ActionResult (never a fabricated SUCCEEDED). type_into_control refuses append-mode on password fields (would require reading the current value -- the exact scraping this design avoids); replace-mode is allowed. An unknown/expired control_id raises SkillExecutionError (-> a real FAILED ActionResult) rather than silently no-opping.
skills/registry.py: desktop_control added to the eager SKILLS dict (stateless aside from its own bounded ControlHandleCache, same category as windows_app/filesystem/browser/terminal).

actions/permissions.py: _KNOWN_ACTION_POLICY['desktop_control'] -- inspect_current_window/list_controls/read_selected_text/read_clipboard = READ_ONLY; focus_control/scroll_control = LOW_RISK; invoke_control/type_into_control/select_control = CONFIRM_REQUIRED. This explicit policy is required, not a convenience: the permission engine's generic state-changing-verb regex does not match invoke_control/type_into_control/select_control, so without this entry those three would incorrectly default to READ_ONLY -- verified directly in tests/test_skill_desktop_control.py::test_classify_risk_covers_every_capability.

known_gaps: The Rust/native-shell side (apps/web/src-tauri/, Antigravity's ownership per AGENTS.md) is untouched by design -- get_active_window_context() there still only captures executable/title/bounds. The new window_state/monitor/focused_control/source schema fields are additive and safe to send once wired from Rust, but nothing currently populates them on the passive per-ActionRequest active_context path; only this session's own inspect_current_window action (which queries live Windows state directly) populates them today. Wiring the Tauri side would cross ownership boundaries and was intentionally left for Antigravity.

invoke_control's Invoke/Toggle/LegacyIAccessiblePattern fallback chain has no coordinate-click fallback, and type_into_control's ValuePattern/LegacyIAccessiblePattern has no keystroke-simulation fallback, both by design per the spec ('do not use blind coordinates when a semantic UI Automation target exists'). A control that genuinely exposes none of the supported patterns fails honestly (SkillExecutionError) rather than falling back to simulation. Not exercised against such a control this session -- every Notepad control tested supported at least one of the intended patterns.

select_control's LegacyIAccessiblePattern fallback path (used only when SelectionItemPattern is unavailable) was not independently exercised this session -- Notepad's TabItemControls all support SelectionItemPattern directly, so only the primary path was verified against a real control.

File Explorer and Settings were not verified this session (real-app testing focused on Notepad end-to-end: enumeration, focus, invoke, type, select, scroll, read-text, read-clipboard, all genuinely exercised there). Both were reviewed as targets during design (standard UIA trees) but a follow-up targeted check against File Explorer's list-view virtualization specifically would be worthwhile before relying on it there.

No multi-step workflow orchestration was built, intentionally -- Codex owns orchestration/control runtime per the spec, and this session must not create an independent agent loop. The five primitives (inspect/list_controls for inspect+select-target, focus_control for focus, invoke_control/type_into_control/select_control/scroll_control for act, re-calling inspect_current_window/list_controls for verify) are each independently dispatchable through the existing Action Runtime today; composing them into a focus->inspect->select->act->verify sequence is the orchestrator's job.

SetForegroundWindow-based focus (focus_control, and windows_app.focus from Wave 2A) is subject to a pre-existing Windows OS foreground-lock timeout that is intermittent depending on which process last held input focus -- observed once in this session's full-suite run (test_skill_windows_app.py::test_execute_focus_finds_and_focuses_real_window), the same flake Wave 2A's own claude.done.json already flagged for that exact test. Not a regression, not specific to this session's new code.

comtypes==1.4.16 and uiautomation==2.0.29 are new required dependencies (added to requirements.txt, not optional) -- TARS targets Windows only, matching the existing pywin32 core-dependency precedent.
